# Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval

## Original exercise

Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).

> 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
> \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
> \(\mathbb R\).

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
value.conclusion: dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H(E)+1, with R^n×R identified with Euclidean R^(n+1), including n=0.

definitions.type: extended nonnegative diameter of a subset of a metric or extended metric space
definitions.definition: For a subset A of a metric or extended metric space X, diam(A)=sup{dist(x,y):x,y in A}, using extended distance and sup(empty)=0. For bounded subsets of a Euclidean space it is identified with its finite nonnegative real value; diam(empty)=0.

definitions.type: scale contents H^s_delta(A) and unnormalized Hausdorff measure H^s(A), valued in [0,infinity]
definitions.definition:
For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put

\[
H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
 A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
\qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
\]

Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension.

definitions.type: library Hausdorff measure, a measure on a Borel extended metric space for each real exponent
definitions.definition: For an extended metric space X with its Borel measurable structure and real a, μH[a] denotes the native MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a, defined as mkMetric(r↦r^a). Here mkMetric is the Borel measure associated to the metric outer measure obtained by taking the supremum over positive diameter scales of the outer measures generated by costs on sets of diameter at most that scale. Empty sets have zero cost. This uses the native extended-real-power convention at a=0. Values on arbitrary subsets are outer-measure values. Its explicit countable-cover formula is invoked as a source theorem in the proof.

binders.type: extended metric space with Borel measurable structure

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of a subset of an extended metric space, valued in [0,infinity]
definitions.definition: dim_H(A) is the native Hausdorff dimension dimH A: with the Borel structure it is sup{a : a is a nonnegative real and μH[a](A)=infinity}, where the supremum is taken in [0,infinity] and sup(empty)=0. Thus dim_H(empty)=0. This is the usual Hausdorff dimension. The proof identifies μH with the supplied unnormalized measure H on Euclidean spaces at every positive exponent; the zero exponent can contribute only the value zero to this supremum.
I=[0,1], with the usual Euclidean distance.

F=E×I. The coordinate identification (x,t)↦(x_1,...,x_n,t) identifies R^n×R with R^(n+1); throughout this product has Euclidean distance sqrt(||x-y||_2^2+|t-u|^2). In particular R^0 is the one-point Euclidean space and this formula also applies when n=0.
D=dim_H(E), initially an extended nonnegative real. Its finiteness is proved before any use of its real value; after that proof it is identified with the corresponding finite nonnegative real.

definitions.type: Lebesgue measure on the Borel real line
definitions.definition: λ is Lebesgue measure on R. Write |J|=λ(J), λ|I for its restriction to I, and ∫_I g dλ for the nonnegative (extended-valued) Lebesgue integral with respect to λ|I. Intervals have their usual Lebesgue lengths.

definitions.type: indicator function with values zero and one
definitions.definition: indicator_J(t)=1 when t∈J and 0 otherwise. This notation is used also as 1_J(t), with nonnegative real or extended nonnegative real values as appropriate.

value.representation_notes: n:ℕ encodes all nonnegative ambient dimensions, including zero. YEuclid m is EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)=PiLp 2 (fun _ : Fin m => ℝ); the 2 is the Lp metric exponent in ℝ≥0∞, not the number of coordinates. Ordinary function/product types have a different metric, so yProd E lives directly in YEuclid (n+1). yHoriz uses Fin.castSucc for the first n coordinates, yVert uses Fin.last n for the last, and yJoin uses Fin.snoc. The proof workers must check yHoriz(yJoin x t)=x, yVert(yJoin x t)=t, yJoin(yHoriz z)(yVert z)=z and the squared-distance formula when used; none is hidden in a definition. yI is the usual scalar [0,1]; this is the canonical scalar presentation of R^1 in the source's one-dimensional specializations. N001 explicitly carries this specialization as well as its coordinate-space family, each proved by the same supplied cover argument, without needing an auxiliary representation transfer. Metric.ediam is the supremum of extended pairwise distances, zero for empty sets. yContent uses ℕ-sequences (finite families padded by empty sets), an indexed infimum over coverage and diameter proofs, and a nonnegative extended tsum. yHaus is the supremum over positive real scales. These are used only at positive exponents, so empty members have zero rpow cost. A missing admissible cover has infimum top. dimH is the pinned native ℝ≥0∞ Hausdorff dimension using its internal Borel structure and the supremum of nonnegative NNReal exponents with infinite native measure; it is not coerced to a real before finiteness is proved. ENNReal.ofReal embeds nonnegative real scales/exponents and truncates negative inputs, so every such use is guarded by positivity. Native critical-exponent APIs take NNReal exponents; use ⟨s,le_of_lt hs⟩. Finite diameters and D may be converted using .toReal only with an explicit not-top fact and ENNReal.ofReal_toReal. yCritical is merely a conjunction defining the exact obligations, not a proved property or premise. All M facts are direct pinned-library uses; Audit A notes remain optional references and add no ports.

steps.statement: (∀ m : ℕ, yCritical (YEuclid m)) ∧ yCritical ℝ
steps.explanation: N001. Instantiate the supplied countable-cover formula directly from Mathlib, first for YEuclid m and also for the scalar model ℝ of R^1. Compare finite positive real scales with extended scales; the infinity-scale term is dominated by scale 1. Positive s makes the empty-set rpow zero. Transfer the four critical-exponent implications using NNReal exponent ⟨s, le_of_lt hs⟩; ENNReal.ofReal s is that exponent's extended value. Nonnegativity holds for every set. The scalar clause is the same one-dimensional specialization, not a new assumption or a dimension theorem.

steps.statement: dimH E < ⊤ ∧ 0 ≤ dimH E ∧ dimH E ≤ (n : ℝ≥0∞) ∧ (n = 0 → E = Set.univ ∧ (∃ x : YEuclid n, E = {x}) ∧ dimH E = 0) ∧ (∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → yContent s δ E < ⊤)
steps.explanation: N002. Preserve the bounded coordinate box and mesh-cube argument for the dimension bound, the separate n=0 singleton branch, and the compact finite-ball cover argument for finite scale contents. Keep dimensions extended-valued until this finiteness result; later use of .toReal must cite this result and ENNReal.ofReal_toReal.

steps.statement: dimH yI ≤ 1 ∧ (∀ a : ℝ, 1 < a → yHaus a yI = 0)
steps.explanation: R003 upper subargument: use N equal-length closed intervals, cost N^(1-a), then take arbitrarily fine covers and the N001 scalar critical fact. Do not replace this route by a precomputed interval-dimension theorem.

steps.statement: ∀ (δ : ℝ), 0 < δ → ∀ V : ℕ → Set ℝ, yCover δ yI V → (1 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ ∑' i, Metric.ediam (V i)
steps.explanation: R003 length-cover subargument: finite diameters imply bounded nonempty members; enlarge their infimum/supremum intervals with widths ε*2^(-i-1), leave empty members empty, and use countable subadditivity of Lebesgue length. Let ε decrease to zero, separating an infinite series. No covering set is assumed measurable.

steps.statement: dimH yI = 1 ∧ (∀ a : ℝ, 1 < a → yHaus a yI = 0) ∧ (∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s < 1 → yHaus s yI = ⊤)
steps.explanation: N003. For 0<s<1 derive the termwise lower bound from diam≤δ, handling zero diameters separately, and sum using T004. Infimum over covers gives content≥δ^(s-1), so its supremum is infinity. Use N001 for the dimension lower bound as s approaches 1; combine with T003.

R004 zero-ambient branch. Under n=0, N002 gives the unique horizontal coordinate and D=0. Push scalar interval covers along t↦yJoin x t; show distances unchanged directly from the Euclidean squared-distance formula. Use the interval zero-measure assertions and N001, then let a decrease to 1.

steps.statement: 1 ≤ n → ∀ (q r ε : ℝ), 0 < q → dimH E < ENNReal.ofReal q → 0 < r → r ≤ 1 → 0 < ε → ∃ U : ℕ → Set (YEuclid n), yCover r E U ∧ (∀ i, (U i).Nonempty → 0 < Metric.ediam (U i)) ∧ yCost q U < ENNReal.ofReal ε
steps.explanation: R004 positive-diameter cover construction. N001 gives zero q-measure and therefore zero r-content. Choose a cover with cost<ε/2 by infimum approximation. Replace each nonempty zero-diameter singleton by a small positive-radius ball of added q-cost≤ε*2^(-i-3), valid since n≥1. Retain empty members with zero cost; this is equivalent to the source's countable nonempty index subset and preserves the chosen sets for the next step.

R004 positive-ambient branch. For q>D and δ>0 choose r=min(1,δ/sqrt 2) and use T007 for arbitrary ε. For each nonempty member of diameter r_i>0, split I into ceil(1/r_i)≤2/r_i intervals. Their images under yJoin cover yProd E, with diameter≤sqrt(2)*r_i by PiLp.dist_sq_eq_of_L2 and Fin's last-coordinate sum decomposition. Empty members contribute no products. Sum the (q+1)-cost bound, let ε→0, take the supremum over δ, apply N001, and let q↓D using T002's finiteness. Any conversion of finite ediam or D to real must prove it is not top first.

steps.statement: dimH (yProd E) ≤ dimH E + 1 ∧ dimH (yProd E) < ⊤
steps.explanation: N004. Split natural n into zero and at least one, combine the two branches, and infer finiteness from finite D+1.

steps.statement: ∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → ∀ V : ℕ → Set (YEuclid (n+1)), yCover δ (yProd E) V → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → yContent s δ E ≤ yCost (s+1) V + ENNReal.ofReal ε
steps.explanation: R005 slicing and integration. Derive horizontal/vertical projection diameter bounds from the Euclidean squared-distance identity (Fin.castSucc and Fin.last). Each rho_i=ediam(V_i) is finite under the scale bound; convert to its real value only with a checked not-top proof. Enclose vertical projections in open J_i of extra length η_i=ε*2^(-i-1)/(1+rho_i^s), empty for empty members. The horizontal projections selected by t∈J_i cover E, giving c≤Σ rho_i^s*1_J_i(t). Show these summands measurable, integrate over volume.restrict yI of mass 1, and apply MeasureTheory.lintegral_tsum with α=ℝ, β=ℕ, μ=volume.restrict yI and explicitly supplied f. The interval length and geometric error bound give the stated inequality, including infinite series. Finite c comes from N002.

steps.statement: ∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → yContent s δ E ≤ yContent (s+1) δ (yProd E)
steps.explanation: N005. For each cover separate an infinite (s+1)-cost; otherwise let arbitrary positive ε decrease to zero in T010. Then take the infimum over all admissible covers of yProd E. No measurability premise is added.

steps.statement: 0 < dimH E → dimH E + 1 ≤ dimH (yProd E)
steps.explanation: N006. For 0<s<D, N001 gives H^s(E)=infinity. The supremum of contents therefore exceeds every finite T at some positive scale; monotonicity under decreasing scale gives the source's arbitrarily small scales. Apply N005, take the product supremum and T→infinity, then N001 yields s+1≤dimH(yProd E). Let s increase to finite D using N002. Real/extended conversions must use finiteness explicitly.

steps.statement: dimH E = 0 → (1 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ dimH (yProd E) ∧ (1 : ℝ≥0∞) = dimH E + 1
steps.explanation: N007. Choose x0∈E. The map t↦yJoin x0 t is isometric for all n, including n=0; prove this with PiLp.dist_sq_eq_of_L2 and the last-coordinate decomposition. Pull each product cover back to an interval cover; pass to infima and suprema to obtain yHaus s yI≤yHaus s (yProd E). For 0<s<1 use N003 and N001, then s↑1. Finally substitute D=0.

P. Finite nonnegative D is either positive or zero; N006 or N007 supplies the lower bound and N004 the upper. Apply antisymmetry. yProd is exactly the coordinate realization of E×[0,1] in the Euclidean (n+1)-space; no change of metric is used.

1: # Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
6: Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
7: Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
8: Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).
9: 
10: > 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
11: > \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
12: > \(\mathbb R\).
13: 
14: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
15: 
16: Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
17: 2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
18: \(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
19: the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.
20: 
21: Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
22: compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
23: with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove
24: 
25: \[
26: \dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
27: \]
28: 
29: The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
30: formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
31: 
32: ## Fixed natural-language proof
33: 
34: For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put
35: 
36: \[
37: H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
38:  A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
39: \qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
40: \]
41: 
42: Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
43: unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use
44: its critical-exponent characterization: \(H^s(A)=0\) if
45: \(s>\dim_H A\), and \(H^s(A)=\infty\) if \(0<s<\dim_H A\).
46: Conversely, zero measure implies \(\dim_H A\leq s\), and infinite
47: measure implies \(\dim_H A\geq s\).
48: 
49: Write \(D=\dim_H E\) and \(F=E\times[0,1]\). First \(0\leq D\leq n\).
50: Indeed, compactness makes \(E\) bounded. When \(n>0\), a box containing
51: it admits a cover by at most \(Ch^{-n}\) cubes of side at most \(h\),
52: for \(0<h\leq1\). Here \(C\) depends only on that box. Each cube has
53: diameter at most \(\sqrt n h\). For any \(s>n\), the total \(s\)-cost
54: is at most \(C n^{s/2}h^{s-n}\to0\). These arbitrarily fine covers
55: give \(H^s(E)=0\) and hence \(D\leq n\). If \(n=0\), nonemptiness
56: makes \(E=\mathbb R^0\), a singleton of zero \(s\)-cost for every
57: \(s>0\); thus \(D=0\).
58: 
59: ### Upper bound
60: 
61: When \(n=0\), \(F\) is isometric to \([0,1]\). Dividing this interval
62: into \(N\) equal pieces gives total \(a\)-cost \(N^{1-a}\to0\) for
63: every \(a>1\), proving \(\dim_H F\leq1=D+1\).
64: For this upper-bound argument now assume \(n\geq1\).
65: 
66: Fix \(q>D\). Since \(q>0\) and \(H^q(E)=0\), for every
67: \(0<r\leq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a countable cover
68: \((U_i)\) of \(E\) with nonempty-member diameters
69: \(0<r_i\leq r\) and \(\sum_i r_i^q<\varepsilon\).
70: The positive-diameter requirement costs nothing: start with a cover of
71: cost below \(\varepsilon/2\); replace each zero-diameter singleton by
72: a ball of diameter at most \(r\), choosing the \(i\)-th replacement
73: to have \(q\)-cost less than \(\varepsilon2^{-i-2}\). The added cost
74: is less than \(\varepsilon/2\). Discard empty members.
75: 
76: Let \(N_i=\lceil1/r_i\rceil\). Partition \([0,1]\) into \(N_i\)
77: closed intervals of length \(1/N_i\leq r_i\). Because \(r_i\leq1\),
78: \(N_i\leq2/r_i\). The corresponding products with \(U_i\) form a
79: countable cover of \(F\). Each has Euclidean diameter at most
80: \(\sqrt2 r_i\), and their total \((q+1)\)-cost is at most
81: 
82: \[
83: \sum_iN_i(\sqrt2 r_i)^{q+1}
84: \leq2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\sum_i r_i^q
85: <2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\varepsilon.
86: \]
87: 
88: For any target scale \(\delta>0\), choose
89: \(r\leq\min(1,\delta/\sqrt2)\), then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
90: Thus \(H^{q+1}_\delta(F)=0\) for every scale, so
91: \(H^{q+1}(F)=0\) and \(\dim_H F\leq q+1\). Letting \(q\downarrow D\)
92: gives \(\dim_H F\leq D+1\).
93: 
94: ### Lower bound when \(D>0\)
95: 
96: Fix \(0<s<D\). Then \(H^s(E)=\infty\), so
97: \(H^s_\delta(E)\) becomes arbitrarily large as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
98: We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\),
99: 
100: \[
101: H^s_\delta(E)\leq H^{s+1}_\delta(F).                 \tag{1}
102: \]
103: 
104: Take an arbitrary countable \(\delta\)-cover \((V_i)_{i\geq0}\) of
105: \(F\), discarding empty members. Define
106: \(\rho_i=\operatorname{diam}V_i\),
107: \(A_i=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(V_i)\), and
108: \(B_i=\pi_{\mathbb R}(V_i)\). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz,
109: so both projected diameters are at most \(\rho_i\leq\delta\).
110: For \(\varepsilon>0\), put
111: 
112: \[
113: \eta_i=\frac{\varepsilon2^{-i-1}}{1+\rho_i^s}>0.
114: \]
115: 
116: Enclose \(B_i\) in an open interval \(J_i\) of length at most
117: \(\rho_i+\eta_i\): its supremum minus infimum is at most \(\rho_i\),
118: and an enlargement of total width \(\eta_i\) suffices. This avoids
119: assuming that the arbitrary covering sets or their projections are measurable.
120: 
121: For each \(t\in[0,1]\), the sets \(A_i\) for which \(t\in J_i\)
122: cover \(E\). Indeed, a point \((x,t)\in F\) belongs to some \(V_i\),
123: giving \(x\in A_i\) and \(t\in B_i\subset J_i\). Their diameters
124: are at most \(\rho_i\). Consequently, with \(c=H^s_\delta(E)\),
125: 
126: \[
127: c\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s\mathbf1_{J_i}(t)\quad(t\in[0,1]).
128: \]
129: 
130: The constant \(c\) is finite: compactness gives a finite cover of \(E\)
131: by balls of diameter at most \(\delta\), with finite \(s\)-cost.
132: Each summand is nonnegative and measurable since \(J_i\) is open.
133: Integrate over \([0,1]\), of Lebesgue measure one, and use Tonelli's
134: theorem for this nonnegative series. Since
135: \(|J_i\cap[0,1]|\leq\rho_i+\eta_i\),
136: 
137: \[
138: \begin{aligned}
139: c&\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s|J_i\cap[0,1]|\\
140:  &\leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\sum_i\eta_i\rho_i^s
141:  \leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\varepsilon.
142: \end{aligned}
143: \]
144: 
145: If the first series is infinite the desired inequality is immediate;
146: otherwise let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Take the infimum over the
147: arbitrary covers to obtain (1). As its left side is unbounded at small
148: scales, \(H^{s+1}(F)=\infty\), giving \(\dim_H F\geq s+1\).
149: Letting \(s\uparrow D\) proves \(\dim_H F\geq D+1\).
150: 
151: ### Lower bound when \(D=0\)
152: 
153: Choose \(x_0\in E\). The map \(t\mapsto(x_0,t)\) is an isometric
154: embedding of \([0,1]\) into \(F\), so dimension monotonicity gives
155: \(\dim_H F\geq\dim_H[0,1]\). This interval has dimension one:
156: equal-length covers gave the upper bound above. For \(0<s<1\), any
157: \(\delta\)-cover with diameters \(\rho_i\leq\delta\) satisfies
158: \(\sum_i\rho_i\geq1\). To see this, enclose its nonempty members
159: in open intervals of lengths at most \(\rho_i+\varepsilon2^{-i-1}\),
160: use countable subadditivity of length to get
161: \(1\leq\sum_i\rho_i+\varepsilon\), and let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
162: Hence \(\sum_i\rho_i^s\geq\delta^{s-1}\sum_i\rho_i
163: \geq\delta^{s-1}\to\infty\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
164: This proves the lower bound one. Thus \(\dim_H F\geq1=D+1\),
165: including when \(n=0\).
166: 
167: Together the bounds establish the required equality.
168:

172: tests. It is a natural-language input, not an NL0 artifact, an Audit A receipt,
173: a Lean proof, or a passing test result. Future runs must independently produce
174: and check those artifacts. The basic Hausdorff-measure and integration facts
175: used here must be registered by that future NL0/Audit A workflow.

import Mathlib
open scoped ENNReal NNReal BigOperators
open Set MeasureTheory
abbrev YEuclid (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)
noncomputable def yContent {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] (s δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) (_ : ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ),
    ∑' i, (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ s
noncomputable def yHaus {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] (s : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (δ : ℝ) (_ : 0 < δ), yContent s δ A
def yI : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
def yHoriz {n : ℕ} (z : YEuclid (n+1)) : YEuclid n :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : Fin n => z i.castSucc)
def yVert {n : ℕ} (z : YEuclid (n+1)) : ℝ := z (Fin.last n)
def yJoin {n : ℕ} (x : YEuclid n) (t : ℝ) : YEuclid (n+1) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.snoc (fun i => x i) t)
def yProd {n : ℕ} (E : Set (YEuclid n)) : Set (YEuclid (n+1)) :=
  {z | yHoriz z ∈ E ∧ yVert z ∈ yI}
def yCritical (X : Type*) [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] : Prop :=
  (∀ A : Set X, 0 ≤ dimH A) ∧
  ∀ (A : Set X) (s : ℝ), 0 < s →
    yHaus s A = MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure s A ∧
    (dimH A < ENNReal.ofReal s → yHaus s A = 0) ∧
    (ENNReal.ofReal s < dimH A → yHaus s A = ⊤) ∧
    (yHaus s A = 0 → dimH A ≤ ENNReal.ofReal s) ∧
    (yHaus s A = ⊤ → ENNReal.ofReal s ≤ dimH A)
def yCover {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] (δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
  A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ
noncomputable def yCost {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] (s : ℝ) (U : ℕ → Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∑' i, (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ s

1: # Audit B: endpoint fidelity and checked Lean closure
2: 
3: The stage-two policy is `endpoint-fidelity-2` (Audit B schema version 2).
4: Its semantic objects are every original external theorem E and the complete
5: final target P. P includes its parameters, quantifiers, hypotheses, domains and
6: conclusion. Accepted NL0/Audit A remains the source authority; B does not repeat
7: unchanged natural-language proof checking.
8: 
9: ## Normal final acceptance and deviation exception
10: 
11: The normal workflow uses `yui-frozen-interface-acceptance-1`. A complete independent
12: pre-proof review establishes source-to-type fidelity for every E and full P and
13: all definitions needed to interpret them. Final native inspection compares the
14: actual exported full types against that frozen contract, checks the exact defining
15: header/pins and semantic receipt, and validates standalone proof/dependency/trust
16: closure. This normal final gate is pure machine work: no additional final LLM is
17: called. It records inherited semantics, not a newly performed independent Audit B.
18: 
19: The actual E/P types include retained hypotheses and quantifiers. Text labels or
20: a source-hash check alone do not establish this gate. The original mathematical
21: review may be wrong; the machine establishes preservation of that reviewed encoding,
22: not correctness of the reviewer's natural-language judgment.
23: 
24: Only complete proof-integrity success plus genuine endpoint/definition drift may
25: open the exceptional independent B-final review below. A faithful result then has
26: `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL`, a freeze-deviation warning and an explicit harness-defect
27: report. Invalid native evidence, incomplete dependencies or changed provenance
28: cannot be overridden semantically. Nonfaithful/unverified results wait for the
29: three explicit user choices in [proof repair](proof-repair.md); accepting a different
30: result does not complete the original target. Explicit/manual legacy semantic
31: receipts remain supported under their original schemas and are not relabeled.
32: Explicitly nonindependent/self-review records remain readable development checks;
33: they cannot grant whole-workflow Audit B acceptance. The same qualification rule
34: applies to supplied Audit A authority and incremental producer/cut reviews.
35: 
36: ## Author correspondence explanations
37: 
38: During interface authoring, provide `endpoint_correspondence`, keyed by every
39: E ID and P. Each entry is `{mode: direct|equivalent, explanation: string}`.
40: Keep it short and useful; do not restate the entire proof or manufacture a
41: line-by-line formalization commentary:
42: 
43: - **Direct:** identify the corresponding variables, hypotheses and assertion.
44:   One sentence is enough when the translation is immediate.
45: - **Equivalent:** explain the mathematical identification or reformulation,
46:   why it works in both directions and which existing conditions it uses.
47:   Point to relevant definitions or checked conversions when needed.
48: 
49: For example, expressing invariance under a finite basis of operators can encode
50: invariance under their linear span: explain the spanning property and closure
51: of a subspace under linear combinations. The review must establish those facts
52: for the actual source algebra/action; the word “equivalent” alone is insufficient.
53: 
54: The postprocessing author carries these notes into each E/P entry in
55: `mapping.json`, checks them against the actual export and completes missing
56: notes for older frozen contracts. It must not change frozen proof statements
57: or bodies merely to improve a note. An explanation is an author's claim, not
58: an Audit B verdict or a formal proof.
59: 
60: ## Semantic responsibility before freeze or at explicit B-final
61: 
62: Read the explanation together with the original source statement and actual
63: elaborated Lean type. Follow the definitions needed to interpret the endpoint,
64: including structure fields that might hide extra assumptions. Check each E/P
65: row, then these four global checks:
66: 
67: 1. `endpoint_inventory_and_scope`: all original E statements and P are covered;
68:    the source version, reviewer scope and inherited qualifications are explicit.
69: 2. `external_statement_fidelity`: each external assumption has the source's
70:    complete mathematical meaning, including conditions and quantifiers. With
71:    no external inputs, record that fact.
72: 3. `complete_target_and_representations`: the entire target theorem has the
73:    same meaning, including every hypothesis. Validate the explanation of each
74:    direct or equivalent encoding and relevant edge cases.
75: 4. `kernel_closure_and_trust`: the actual exported proof compiled, all required
76:    producers and intermediate library ports were discharged, and the checked
77:    root has only the declared external assumptions and permitted foundations.
78: 
79: Equivalent formulations are allowed. Do not reject a faithful encoding because
80: it lacks a particular Mathlib type/name, a separate object for every NL0
81: D node, or a duplicate formal representation. A mathematical source-to-code
82: identification can be checked semantically without constructing an unnecessary
83: second model. If the implementation actually crosses two different Lean
84: representations, the required conversion must occur in checked Lean code.
85: Unexplained equivalence, stronger assumptions, missing hypotheses, changed
86: domains or hidden target assumptions remain defects.
87: 
88: Do not accept an explanation on trust or copy the author's conclusion into the
89: review. Record PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED with specific findings and source/type/note
90: locations. A compiler pass cannot substitute for this independent judgment.
91: 
92: ## Freely available Mathlib
93: 
94: All proved results in the pinned Mathlib environment are available in stage
95: two. Do not compare their names, counts or node-by-node uses with the NL0 M
96: inventory. There is no per-M semantic row, imported-proof whitelist,
97: `calculation_links` ledger, or separate review of implementation N/D nodes.
98: Definitions are examined when they determine endpoint meaning, not for an
99: exact inventory match. Notes from Audit A are optional local guidance, not
100: permissions to use a library theorem.
101: 
102: New interfaces normally use Mathlib directly. An older or deliberately
103: conditional interface can retain M ports; `library_terms` supplies an actual
104: Lean proof for each such port at assembly. These are discharge proofs, not a
105: library correspondence inventory. They cannot remain unproved assumptions of
106: the final export. New external axioms or stronger project hypotheses still
107: require returning to the affected source boundary.
108: 
109: ## Mechanical evidence and limits
110: 
111: ### Compact review materials
112: 
113: The semantic reviewer reads the separately versioned
114: `yui-audit-b-review-view-1` in `review-packet.json`. Start at `/scope` and
115: `/mechanical_summary`, then examine each `/endpoints/<ID>` source, actual
116: inspected type and author correspondence. P retains the complete original
117: target, parameters and hypotheses. The view is a deterministic Python extraction,
118: not an LLM summary or mathematical judgment. It never substitutes a declared
119: expected type for the actual inspected type.
120: 
121: `/documents` identifies hash-bound `source-context.json`, `source-original.txt`
122: and actual `Proof.lean`. Read relevant original and Lean definitions there,
123: including hidden structure fields, when needed to interpret an endpoint.
124: Complete raw compiler, elaboration and dependency records stay in the machine
125: archive; they are not default reviewer inputs. A mechanical summary reports
126: actual checks and exceptions, without populating a semantic PASS. The full
127: dependency inspection remains a program responsibility.
128: 
129: Use `read_task_input` JSON pointers, not guessed fixed line positions. Large
130: containers expose keys and large strings expose `next_offset`. Text reads
131: resume with `next_start` and `next_column`. Serialized read results are at most
132: 32 KiB; follow `has_more` until the needed statement is complete. This pagination
133: limit is not a task time/token/call budget. Unknown calls or modified feedback
134: remain rejected with a specific local protocol fault, not a retryable HTTP 502.
135: 
136: ### Explicit reuse of completed native evidence
137: 
138: `audit_b.py reuse-review <new-directory> --original <old-audit-directory>`
139: prepares a new semantic review without rebuilding or changing Lean. It validates
140: every original input and snapshot, the original native artifacts/output, source
141: and accepted-A authority, environment pins, and the exact historical tool
142: snapshots. The new view and current reviewer runtime are separately bound in
143: `review-reuse.json`; the normal current-build tool check is not disabled.
144: Changed or incomplete evidence blocks reuse. Preserve the original failure.
145: 
146: The new independent reviewer receives no previous B verdict, reviewer history,
147: owner reasoning or other-case material. The receipt discloses inherited native
148: checks and a new semantic review; it cannot claim fresh compilation, an unaided
149: cold whole-workflow success or measured acceleration. Changing proofs or source
150: requires the appropriate new checks, rather than this review-only path.
151: 
152: `audit_b.py prepare/build/check` binds the source, accepted A, contract, plan,
153: proofs, tool versions and environment hashes. Build compiles standalone
154: `Proof.lean` before adding inspection. It checks E/P against their declared
155: encoded types, modulo definitional equality and bijective universe renaming.
156: It does not prove equivalence between natural-language text and Lean.
157: Distinct universes must not be collapsed; changed types or hypotheses must not
158: be normalized away. Source fidelity is established by the bound pre-proof independent review, or an actual exceptional B-final review; this native comparison does not establish it anew.
159: 
160: Inspection follows the actual `AuditBExport.P` closure. No `sorry`, unproved
161: local axiom/opaque substitute or undeclared foundation may be introduced.
162: Local bodies still compile against their own task inputs and the pinned
163: library; every required producer must exist. Assembly, inspection and semantic
164: review have separate recorded outcomes.
165: 
166: Version-1 receipts remain historical results under their original policy.
167: They cannot be silently relabeled or accepted as version-2 reviews. Start a
168: new bound audit when policy, source, code or evidence changes. Pending templates
169: never pass. A whole accepted source plus complete native gates and its bound semantic
170: authority yields `AUDIT-B-PASSED`; a fragment yields at most the explicitly
171: scoped development verdict. A whole source with an actual conditional Audit A
172: can yield `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL` after all the same native and semantic checks.
173: It retains the exact source warnings and never upgrades them to full PASS.
174: Neither proves external publications in Lean or
175: establishes formalizer speedup. Preserve failures and report actual costs.

value.text: Fix m, A and s as declared. Apply M001 to the Euclidean metric space R^m, its Borel measurable structure, exponent s and set A. At each finite positive scale, the formula's covers are exactly the covers in D002: a countable family can be enumerated by natural numbers, padding with empty sets if finite, and conversely a sequence is countable. All nonempty sets allowed at such a scale are bounded, so their extended diameters equal their ordinary finite Euclidean diameters. Empty members have cost zero in both definitions; since s>0, nonempty singletons also have zero cost. Thus the inner infimum is exactly the supplied scale content. The extra scale infinity in M001 adds nothing to the supremum: its admissible covers include all covers at scale 1, so its infimum is at most the scale-1 content. The finite positive extended scales are precisely the positive real scales. Taking their supremum proves F001: H^s(A)=μH[s](A). No dimensional normalization constant is introduced.

Use F001 to transport the four critical-exponent facts. Under L1: 0<s<dim_H(A), M002 with nonnegative exponent a=s gives μH[s](A)=infinity, hence H^s(A)=infinity; discharge L1. Under L2: dim_H(A)<s, M003 gives μH[s](A)=0, hence H^s(A)=0; discharge L2. Under L3: H^s(A)=0, F001 makes μH[s](A)=0≠infinity, and M004 gives dim_H(A)≤s; discharge L3. Under L4: H^s(A)=infinity, F001 and M005 give s≤dim_H(A); discharge L4. These are the complete conditional assertions F002.

The dimension in D004 is a supremum in the nonnegative extended reals, so it is nonnegative, including for the empty set. The arbitrary choices of m,A,s and F001-F002 prove every clause of the output proposition.

By H003, E is compact, hence bounded in its Euclidean metric. A bounded subset of R^n is contained in a coordinate box [-b,b]^n for some b>0: each coordinate distance is at most the Euclidean distance, and increasing a bound if necessary makes it positive. This also holds in R^0. Record F001. H001 specifies the nonnegative ambient dimension; N001 gives D≥0.

Choose b from F001 and define C as declared. Under L1: n>0, fix arbitrary a and h under L2: a>n and L3: 0<h≤1. Divide each coordinate interval [-b,b] into ceil(2b/h) intervals of side at most h. Their number is at most (2b+1)/h in each coordinate, hence the resulting at most C h^(-n) closed cubes cover E. Each cube has Euclidean diameter at most sqrt(n)h. Therefore their total a-cost is at most C h^(-n)(sqrt(n)h)^a=C n^(a/2)h^(a-n). Since a-n>0, this tends to zero as h decreases to zero, and their diameters also tend to zero. In particular, at each fixed target scale arbitrarily small h provides admissible covers with costs tending to zero, so H^a(E)=0. Discharge L3 after using the arbitrary mesh sizes. N001 with A=E, exponent a gives D≤a. Since a>n was arbitrary, D≤n (if D>n, choose a strictly between n and D). Discharge L2 and L1. This proves F002.

Under L4: n=0, Euclidean R^0 consists of its single empty-coordinate point. H002 implies E=R^0. A cover by that singleton has diameter and s-cost zero for every positive exponent s. Thus H^s(E)=0 for all s>0, and N001 gives D≤s for every s>0, whence D=0 using D≥0. Discharge L4. By H001 the alternatives n=0 and n>0 exhaust the ambient dimensions. F002 and this branch give 0≤D≤n, so D is finite, with the stated singleton conclusion when n=0.

Fix arbitrary positive s and delta. The open balls of radius delta/2 centered at the points of E form an open cover. By H003 there is a finite subcover, and each such ball has diameter at most delta. Its finite number of members and finite diameters give a finite total s-cost. The defining infimum therefore gives H^s_delta(E)<infinity. Together with F003 this proves the output proposition.

Fix arbitrary a under L1: a>1. For each positive integer N, divide I into N closed intervals of length 1/N. They have total a-cost N(1/N)^a=N^(1-a), which tends to zero as N tends to infinity, while their maximum diameter tends to zero. Thus at every positive target scale the defining infimum is zero, and H^a(I)=0. N001 applied with ambient dimension 1 gives dim_H(I)≤a; taking a down to 1 gives dim_H(I)≤1. Discharge L1 and record F001, including the universally quantified zero-measure assertion.

Fix delta>0 and an arbitrary sequence V under L2: V is a delta-cover of I. Define rho as declared; each rho_i≤delta is finite. Fix epsilon>0 and define J as declared. A nonempty V_i is bounded, so its real supremum and infimum exist and sup(V_i)-inf(V_i)=rho_i. Therefore V_i⊆J_i and |J_i|≤rho_i+epsilon*2^(-i-1), also when V_i is empty. The open sets J_i cover I. Countable subadditivity of Lebesgue measure and |I|=1 give 1≤sum_i |J_i|≤sum_i rho_i+epsilon, using sum_{i≥0}2^(-i-1)=1. If sum_i rho_i is infinite the required inequality is immediate; if finite, letting the arbitrary epsilon decrease to zero yields F002: sum_i rho_i≥1. All sets measured here are open intervals or I, so no measurability of V_i is assumed.

Fix arbitrary s under L3: 0<s<1. For each i with rho_i>0, rho_i≤delta and s-1<0 give rho_i^s=rho_i*rho_i^(s-1)≥delta^(s-1)*rho_i. The inequality also holds when rho_i=0 since s>0. Summing nonnegative terms and using F002 gives sum_i rho_i^s≥delta^(s-1)sum_i rho_i≥delta^(s-1). Since V was an arbitrary delta-cover, taking the infimum gives H^s_delta(I)≥delta^(s-1). Discharge L2 in this universal cover conclusion. Since delta>0 was arbitrary and delta^(s-1) tends to infinity as delta decreases to zero, H^s(I)=infinity. N001 gives dim_H(I)≥s. Let s increase to 1 to get dim_H(I)≥1, and discharge L3. Together with F001 this is dim_H(I)=1 and all the measure assertions of the output proposition.

Under L1: n=0, N002 gives E=R^0 and D=0. The coordinate map from I to F obtained by adjoining the unique R^0 coordinate preserves all distances. Fix arbitrary a under L4: a>1. N003 gives H^a(I)=0, so by the defining infimum there are covers of I at every positive scale with arbitrarily small a-cost. Push these covers forward by that coordinate map; their diameters are unchanged, so H^a(F)=0. N001 gives dim_H(F)≤a. Let the arbitrary a decrease to 1 to obtain dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. Discharge L4 and L1 and record F000.

For the other branch introduce L2: n≥1. Fix arbitrary q under L3: q>D, and arbitrary positive delta and epsilon. N002 gives D≥0, so q>0. Define r=min(1,delta/sqrt(2))>0; thus r≤1 and sqrt(2)r≤delta. By N001 applied to E, H^q(E)=0. The nonnegative content H^q_r(E) is at most this supremum, hence zero. The infimum defining that content therefore supplies a countable r-cover W with total q-cost<epsilon/2. The infimum is zero, so its admissible family is nonempty (an empty infimum is infinity); its defining approximation property gives the stated cover. This is the existence statement F001, before choosing W.

Choose W from F001. Define beta,U,K,r_i as declared. A nonempty zero-diameter Euclidean set is a singleton. Because n≥1, its replacement open ball has positive diameter beta_i≤r and q-cost beta_i^q≤epsilon*2^(-i-3)<epsilon*2^(-i-2). Nonempty positive-diameter members are unchanged; every point originally covered remains covered. The additional cost is at most sum_{i≥0}epsilon*2^(-i-3)=epsilon/4<epsilon/2. Thus, after discarding empty members by restricting to K, U is a countable cover of E with 0<r_i≤r and sum_{i∈K}r_i^q<epsilon. This is F002; the countable index set may be finite.

For i∈K define N_i=ceil(1/r_i). Divide I into N_i closed intervals, each of length 1/N_i≤r_i. Since r_i≤1, N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i. The products of U_i with these intervals form a countable cover of F. The Euclidean distance formula in D006 shows that every product member has diameter at most sqrt(2)r_i≤sqrt(2)r≤delta. Their total (q+1)-cost is bounded by
sum_(i∈K) N_i (sqrt(2)r_i)^(q+1)
≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1) sum_(i∈K) r_i^q
<2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon.
These inequalities follow termwise from N_i≤2/r_i and then by nonnegative summation, so they remain valid for countably many members. Consequently H^(q+1)_delta(F)≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon, which is F003.

For fixed q and delta, epsilon>0 was arbitrary; the content in F003 is independent of epsilon, so it is zero. Since delta>0 was arbitrary, H^(q+1)(F)=0. N001, with ambient dimension n+1 and positive exponent q+1, gives dim_H(F)≤q+1. Since q>D was arbitrary and D is finite by N002, let q decrease to D to obtain dim_H(F)≤D+1: an alleged strict excess would allow a q between D and dim_H(F)-1, contradicting this bound (an infinite dimension is already excluded by any one q>D). Discharge L3 and L2. This proves F004.
A natural dimension n is either zero or at least one. F000 and F004 thus give dim_H(F)≤D+1 in all cases. By N002 the right hand side is finite, proving the finiteness clause as well.

Fix s>0, delta>0 and an arbitrary sequence V under L1: V covers F and diam(V_i)≤delta for all i. Empty members may be discarded; equivalently retain them with all ensuing projections and intervals empty and costs zero. Define rho,A_i,B_i and c as declared. Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz for the Euclidean metric in D006: each squared coordinate distance is bounded by the sum of the squared horizontal and vertical distances. Hence diam(A_i),diam(B_i)≤rho_i≤delta. In particular a nonempty B_i is a nonempty bounded subset of R. N002 applies to the positive s,delta and gives c<infinity.

Fix arbitrary epsilon>0 and set eta_i=epsilon*2^(-i-1)/(1+rho_i^s)>0. Define J as declared. For a nonempty B_i, its supremum minus its infimum equals its diameter and is at most rho_i by F001. Thus B_i⊆J_i and |J_i|≤rho_i+eta_i. The empty-member convention makes both assertions true for empty V_i as well. The J_i are open measurable sets and enclose the possibly nonmeasurable projections. This construction needs no measurability of V_i,A_i or B_i.

Define the nonnegative functions f_i(t)=rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t). They are measurable because each J_i is open and each coefficient is a fixed finite nonnegative real. Under L2: t∈I, for every x∈E the point (x,t) lies in F, so some V_i contains it. Then x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. Thus the family of A_i with t∈J_i is a delta-cover of E, and the defining infimum and diam(A_i)≤rho_i give c≤sum_i rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t)=sum_i f_i(t). The point x here is universally bound in this coverage argument, and i is its existential cover index. Discharge L2 into the assertion for every t∈I. Record F003.

Set μ=λ|I. It is a measure on the Borel real line with μ(R)=λ(I)=1. Apply M006 with α=R, its Borel structure, index type β=N, this measure μ and the functions f of F003. Borel measurability implies μ-almost-everywhere measurability for each summand. Monotonicity of the nonnegative integral and the integral of a constant on a set of measure one give
c≤∫_I sum_i f_i(t) dλ
 =sum_i ∫_I f_i(t) dλ
 =sum_i rho_i^s |J_i∩I|
 ≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+sum_i eta_i rho_i^s
 ≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+epsilon.
Here the middle equality is the integral of a measurable indicator times its nonnegative coefficient. The first inequality inside the sum uses F002 and distributivity of nonnegative sums. Finally eta_i rho_i^s=epsilon*2^(-i-1)*rho_i^s/(1+rho_i^s)≤epsilon*2^(-i-1), whose sum is epsilon. All sums and integrals are nonnegative and may be infinite; c is finite by F001. This is F004.

If sum_i rho_i^(s+1)=infinity, c≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1) holds immediately. Otherwise F004 holds for every epsilon>0 with c and V fixed, so letting epsilon decrease to zero gives the same inequality c≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1). The cover V was arbitrary under L1. Take the infimum over all its possible delta-covers of F and discharge L1, obtaining H^s_delta(E)≤H^(s+1)_delta(F). Since s>0 and delta>0 were arbitrary, this is precisely the output proposition.

Temporarily assume L1: D>0 and L2: 0<s<D for arbitrary real s. N001 gives H^s(E)=infinity. Fix any T>0. By the definition of H^s as the supremum of the scale contents, there exists a positive delta with H^s_delta(E)>T; otherwise their supremum would be at most the finite T. Moreover these contents are nondecreasing as scale decreases, since a cover admissible at a smaller scale is admissible at any larger one. Thus any such bound remains valid on decreasing its scale, so the contents become arbitrarily large at arbitrarily small scales. Record the existence F001 before making a choice.

Choose delta from F001. N005 applies to the positive s and delta and gives H^(s+1)_delta(F)≥H^s_delta(E)>T. Taking the supremum defining H^(s+1)(F) yields H^(s+1)(F)>T. This is F002, independent of the chosen scale.
Since F002 holds for the arbitrary positive finite T, H^(s+1)(F)=infinity. N001 applies with ambient dimension n+1 and exponent s+1>0, giving dim_H(F)≥s+1. Record F003.

By N002, D is finite; under L1 it is positive. F003 holds for every s with 0<s<D. Such s can increase to D, so their s+1 have supremum D+1 and dim_H(F)≥D+1. Equivalently every real number below D+1 is below some s+1 with 0<s<D. Discharge L2 in this universal limiting argument and then L1, obtaining the complete conditional output.

Temporarily assume L1: D=0. By H002 choose x_0∈E and define f(t)=(x_0,t). The Euclidean metric formula in D006 gives dist(f(t),f(u))=|t-u| for all real t,u, including n=0. Thus f restricts to an isometric embedding of I into F.

Fix arbitrary s under L2: 0<s<1. For any delta>0 and arbitrary V under L3: V is a delta-cover of F, define W as declared. F001 shows W covers I, and isometry gives diam(W_i)≤diam(V_i)≤delta. Hence H^s_delta(I)≤sum_i diam(V_i)^s. Take the infimum over V, discharge L3, and then take the supremum over positive delta to get H^s(I)≤H^s(F). This proves the particular dimension-monotonicity implication used here directly from covers. N003 gives H^s(I)=infinity, so H^s(F)=infinity. N001 applied to F and exponent s yields dim_H(F)≥s.

Since F002 holds for every s with 0<s<1, letting s increase to 1 gives dim_H(F)≥1. Discharge L2. Under L1, 1=D+1, so this proves the asserted bound. Discharge L1 to obtain the output proposition. The argument used only the isometric embedding from a point of E, and applies unchanged to the singleton ambient space R^0.

N002 gives finite D≥0. Thus either D>0 or D=0. In the positive case N006 gives dim_H(F)≥D+1; in the zero case N007 gives the identical bound, including n=0. N004 supplies dim_H(F)≤D+1 in all cases. Antisymmetry gives dim_H(F)=D+1. Substituting F=E×[0,1] and D=dim_H(E), with the Euclidean identification of D006, proves the complete target P.

value.text: Under L1: n=0, N002 gives E=R^0 and D=0. The coordinate map from I to F obtained by adjoining the unique R^0 coordinate preserves all distances. Fix arbitrary a under L4: a>1. N003 gives H^a(I)=0, so by the defining infimum there are covers of I at every positive scale with arbitrarily small a-cost. Push these covers forward by that coordinate map; their diameters are unchanged, so H^a(F)=0. N001 gives dim_H(F)≤a. Let the arbitrary a decrease to 1 to obtain dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. Discharge L4 and L1 and record F000.

value.text: For the other branch introduce L2: n≥1. Fix arbitrary q under L3: q>D, and arbitrary positive delta and epsilon. N002 gives D≥0, so q>0. Define r=min(1,delta/sqrt(2))>0; thus r≤1 and sqrt(2)r≤delta. By N001 applied to E, H^q(E)=0. The nonnegative content H^q_r(E) is at most this supremum, hence zero. The infimum defining that content therefore supplies a countable r-cover W with total q-cost<epsilon/2. The infimum is zero, so its admissible family is nonempty (an empty infimum is infinity); its defining approximation property gives the stated cover. value.text: Choose W from F001. Define beta,U,K,r_i as declared. A nonempty zero-diameter Euclidean set is a singleton. Because n≥1, its replacement open ball has positive diameter beta_i≤r and q-cost beta_i^q≤epsilon*2^(-i-3)<epsilon*2^(-i-2). Nonempty positive-diameter members are unchanged; every point originally covered remains covered. The additional cost is at most sum_{i≥0}epsilon*2^(-i-3)=epsilon/4<epsilon/2. Thus, after discarding empty members by restricting to K, U is a countable cover of E with 0<r_i≤r and sum_{i∈K}r_i^q<epsilon. This is F002; the countable index set may be finite.

value.text:
For i∈K define N_i=ceil(1/r_i). Divide I into N_i closed intervals, each of length 1/N_i≤r_i. Since r_i≤1, N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i. The products of U_i with these intervals form a countable cover of F. The Euclidean distance formula in D006 shows that every product member has diameter at most sqrt(2)r_i≤sqrt(2)r≤delta. Their total (q+1)-cost is bounded by
sum_(i∈K) N_i (sqrt(2)r_i)^(q+1)
≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1) sum_(i∈K) r_i^q
<2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon.
These inequalities follow termwise from N_i≤2/r_i and then by nonnegative summation, so they remain valid for countably many members. Consequently H^(q+1)_delta(F)≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon, which is F003.

value.text: For fixed q and delta, epsilon>0 was arbitrary; the content in F003 is independent of epsilon, so it is zero. Since delta>0 was arbitrary, H^(q+1)(F)=0. 80: then `Π i, f i` is an inner product space as well. Since `Π i, f i` is endowed with the sup norm,
81: we use instead `PiLp 2 f` for the product space, which is endowed with the `L^2` norm.

83: instance PiLp.innerProductSpace {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : ι → Type*)
84:     [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (f i)] [∀ i, InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (f i)] :
85:     InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (PiLp 2 f) where
86:   inner x y := ∑ i, ⟪x i, y i⟫
87:   norm_sq_eq_re_inner x := by
88:     simp only [PiLp.norm_sq_eq_of_L2, map_sum, ← norm_sq_eq_re_inner]
89:   conj_inner_symm := by
90:     intro x y
91:     unfold inner
92:     rw [map_sum]
93:     apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
94:     rintro z -
95:     apply inner_conj_symm
96:   add_left x y z :=
97:     show (∑ i, ⟪x i + y i, z i⟫ = ∑ i, ⟪x i, z i⟫ + ∑ i, ⟪y i, z i⟫) by
98:       simp only [inner_add_left, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
99:   smul_left x y r :=
100:     show (∑ i : ι, ⟪r • x i, y i⟫ = conj r * ∑ i, ⟪x i, y i⟫) by

104:     [∀ i, InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (f i)] (x y : PiLp 2 f) : ⟪x, y⟫ = ∑ i, ⟪x i, y i⟫ :=

107: /-- The standard real/complex Euclidean space, functions on a finite type. For an `n`-dimensional
108: space use `EuclideanSpace 𝕜 (Fin n)`.
109: 
110: For the case when `n = Fin _`, there is `!₂[x, y, ...]` notation for building elements of this type,
111: analogous to `![x, y, ...]` notation. -/
112: @[wikidata Q17295]
113: abbrev EuclideanSpace (𝕜 : Type*) (n : Type*) : Type _ :=
114:   PiLp 2 fun _ : n => 𝕜

120: /-- Notation for vectors in Lp space. `!₂[x, y, ...]` is a shorthand for
121: `WithLp.toLp 2 ![x, y, ...]`, of type `EuclideanSpace _ (Fin _)`.
122: 
123: This also works for other subscripts. -/
124: syntax (name := PiLp.vecNotation) "!" noWs subscriptTerm noWs "[" term,* "]" : term
125: macro_rules | `(!$p:subscript[$e:term,*]) => do

131: @[app_delab WithLp.toLp]

133:   whenNotPPOption getPPExplicit <| whenPPOption getPPNotation <| withOverApp 3 do
134:     -- check that the `WithLp.toLp _` is present
135:     let p : Term ← withNaryArg 0 <| delab
136:     -- to be conservative, only allow subscripts which are numerals

66: We use the following notation localized in `MeasureTheory`. It is defined in
67: `MeasureTheory.Measure.Hausdorff`.

69: - `μH[d]` : `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure d`
70: 
71: ## Implementation notes
72: 
73: * The definition of `dimH` explicitly uses `borel X` as a measurable space structure. This way we
74:   can formulate lemmas about Hausdorff dimension without assuming that the environment has a
75:   `[MeasurableSpace X]` instance that is equal but possibly not defeq to `borel X`.
76: 
77:   Lemma `dimH_def` unfolds this definition using whatever `[MeasurableSpace X]` instance we have in
78:   the environment (as long as it is equal to `borel X`).
79: 
80: * The definition `dimH` is irreducible; use API lemmas or `dimH_def` instead.
81: 
82: ## Tags
83: 
84: Hausdorff measure, Hausdorff dimension, dimension
85: -/

96: /-- Hausdorff dimension of a set in an (e)metric space. -/
97: @[irreducible] noncomputable def dimH (s : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ := by
98:   borelize X; exact ⨆ (d : ℝ≥0) (_ : @hausdorffMeasure X _ _ ⟨rfl⟩ d s = ∞), d
99:

101: ### Basic properties
102: -/

105: section Measurable
106: 
107: variable [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]
108: 
109: /-- Unfold the definition of `dimH` using `[MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]` from the
110: environment. -/
111: theorem dimH_def (s : Set X) : dimH s = ⨆ (d : ℝ≥0) (_ : μH[d] s = ∞), (d : ℝ≥0∞) := by
112:   borelize X; rw [dimH]
113: 
114: theorem hausdorffMeasure_of_lt_dimH {s : Set X} {d : ℝ≥0} (h : ↑d < dimH s) : μH[d] s = ∞ := by
115:   simp only [dimH_def, lt_iSup_iff] at h
116:   rcases h with ⟨d', hsd', hdd'⟩
117:   rw [ENNReal.coe_lt_coe, ← NNReal.coe_lt_coe] at hdd'
118:   exact top_unique (hsd' ▸ hausdorffMeasure_mono hdd'.le _)
119: 
120: theorem dimH_le {s : Set X} {d : ℝ≥0∞} (H : ∀ d' : ℝ≥0, μH[d'] s = ∞ → ↑d' ≤ d) : dimH s ≤ d :=
121:   (dimH_def s).trans_le <| iSup₂_le H
122: 
123: theorem dimH_le_of_hausdorffMeasure_ne_top {s : Set X} {d : ℝ≥0} (h : μH[d] s ≠ ∞) : dimH s ≤ d :=
124:   le_of_not_gt <| mt hausdorffMeasure_of_lt_dimH h
125: 
126: theorem le_dimH_of_hausdorffMeasure_eq_top {s : Set X} {d : ℝ≥0} (h : μH[d] s = ∞) :
127:     ↑d ≤ dimH s := by
128:   rw [dimH_def]; exact le_iSup₂ (α := ℝ≥0∞) d h
129: 
130: theorem hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt {s : Set X} {d : ℝ≥0} (h : dimH s < d) : μH[d] s = 0 := by
131:   rw [dimH_def] at h
132:   rcases ENNReal.lt_iff_exists_nnreal_btwn.1 h with ⟨d', hsd', hd'd⟩
133:   rw [ENNReal.coe_lt_coe, ← NNReal.coe_lt_coe] at hd'd
134:   exact (hausdorffMeasure_zero_or_top hd'd s).resolve_right fun h₂ => hsd'.not_ge <|
135:     le_iSup₂ (α := ℝ≥0∞) d' h₂
136: 
137: theorem measure_zero_of_dimH_lt {μ : Measure X} {d : ℝ≥0} (h : μ ≪ μH[d]) {s : Set X}
138:     (hd : dimH s < d) : μ s = 0 :=
139:   h <| hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt hd
140: 
141: theorem le_dimH_of_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero {s : Set X} {d : ℝ≥0} (h : μH[d] s ≠ 0) : ↑d ≤ dimH s :=
142:   le_of_not_gt <| mt hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt h
143: 
144: theorem dimH_of_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero_ne_top {d : ℝ≥0} {s : Set X} (h : μH[d] s ≠ 0)
145:     (h' : μH[d] s ≠ ∞) : dimH s = d :=
146:   le_antisymm (dimH_le_of_hausdorffMeasure_ne_top h') (le_dimH_of_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero h)
147: 
148: /-- The Hausdorff dimension of a set `s` is the infimum of all `d : ℝ≥0` such that the
149: `d`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of `s` is zero. This infimum is taken in `ℝ≥0∞`.
150: This gives an equivalent definition of the Hausdorff dimension. -/
151: theorem dimH_eq_iInf (s : Set X) : dimH s = ⨅ (d : ℝ≥0) (_ : μH[d] s = 0), (d : ℝ≥0∞) := by
152:   apply le_antisymm
153:   · rw [dimH_def]
154:     simp only [le_iInf_iff, iSup_le_iff, ENNReal.coe_le_coe]
155:     intro i hi j hj
156:     by_contra! hij
157:     simpa [hi, hj] using hausdorffMeasure_mono hij.le s
158:   · by_contra! h
159:     rcases ENNReal.lt_iff_exists_nnreal_btwn.1 h with ⟨d', hdim_lt, hlt⟩
160:     have h0 : μH[d'] s = 0 := hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt hdim_lt
161:     exact hlt.not_ge (iInf₂_le d' h0)
162: 
163: end Measurable

165: @[gcongr, mono]
166: theorem dimH_mono {s t : Set X} (h : s ⊆ t) : dimH s ≤ dimH t := by
167:   borelize X
168:   exact dimH_le fun d hd => le_dimH_of_hausdorffMeasure_eq_top <| top_unique <| hd ▸ measure_mono h
169: 
170: theorem dimH_subsingleton {s : Set X} (h : s.Subsingleton) : dimH s = 0 := by
171:   borelize X
172:   rw [← nonpos_iff_eq_zero]
173:   apply dimH_le_of_hausdorffMeasure_ne_top
174:   exact ((hausdorffMeasure_le_one_of_subsingleton h le_rfl).trans_lt ENNReal.one_lt_top).ne
175: 
176: alias Set.Subsingleton.dimH_zero := dimH_subsingleton
177: 
178: @[simp]
179: theorem dimH_empty : dimH (∅ : Set X) = 0 :=
180:   subsingleton_empty.dimH_zero
181: 
182: @[simp]
183: theorem dimH_singleton (x : X) : dimH ({x} : Set X) = 0 :=
184:   subsingleton_singleton.dimH_zero
185: 
186: @[simp]
187: theorem dimH_iUnion {ι : Sort*} [Countable ι] (s : ι → Set X) :
188:     dimH (⋃ i, s i) = ⨆ i, dimH (s i) := by
189:   borelize X
190:   refine le_antisymm (dimH_le fun d hd => ?_) (iSup_le fun i => dimH_mono <| subset_iUnion _ _)
191:   contrapose! hd
192:   have : ∀ i, μH[d] (s i) = 0 := fun i =>
193:     hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt ((le_iSup (fun i => dimH (s i)) i).trans_lt hd)
194:   rw [measure_iUnion_null this]
195:   exact ENNReal.zero_ne_top
196: 
197: @[simp]
198: theorem dimH_bUnion {s : Set ι} (hs : s.Countable) (t : ι → Set X) :
199:     dimH (⋃ i ∈ s, t i) = ⨆ i ∈ s, dimH (t i) := by
200:   haveI := hs.toEncodable
201:   rw [biUnion_eq_iUnion, dimH_iUnion, ← iSup_subtype'']
202: 
203: @[simp]
204: theorem dimH_sUnion {S : Set (Set X)} (hS : S.Countable) : dimH (⋃₀ S) = ⨆ s ∈ S, dimH s := by
205:   rw [sUnion_eq_biUnion, dimH_bUnion hS]
206: 
207: @[simp]
208: theorem dimH_union (s t : Set X) : dimH (s ∪ t) = max (dimH s) (dimH t) := by
209:   rw [union_eq_iUnion, dimH_iUnion, iSup_bool_eq, cond, cond]
210: 
211: theorem dimH_countable {s : Set X} (hs : s.Countable) : dimH s = 0 :=
212:   biUnion_of_singleton s ▸ by simp only [dimH_bUnion hs, dimH_singleton, ENNReal.iSup_zero]
213: 
214: alias Set.Countable.dimH_zero := dimH_countable

496: /-- To bound the Hausdorff measure (or, more generally, for a measure defined using
497: `MeasureTheory.Measure.mkMetric`) of a set, one may use coverings with maximum diameter tending to
498: `0`, indexed by any sequence of countable types. -/
499: theorem mkMetric_le_liminf_tsum {β : Type*} {ι : β → Type*} [∀ n, Countable (ι n)] (s : Set X)
500:     {l : Filter β} (r : β → ℝ≥0∞) (hr : Tendsto r l (𝓝 0)) (t : ∀ n : β, ι n → Set X)
501:     (ht : ∀ᶠ n in l, ∀ i, ediam (t n i) ≤ r n) (hst : ∀ᶠ n in l, s ⊆ ⋃ i, t n i) (m : ℝ≥0∞ → ℝ≥0∞) :
502:     mkMetric m s ≤ liminf (fun n => ∑' i, m (ediam (t n i))) l := by
503:   haveI : ∀ n, Encodable (ι n) := fun n => Encodable.ofCountable _
504:   simp only [mkMetric_apply]
505:   refine iSup₂_le fun ε hε => ?_
506:   refine le_of_forall_gt_imp_ge_of_dense fun c hc => ?_
507:   rcases ((frequently_lt_of_liminf_lt (by isBoundedDefault) hc).and_eventually
508:         ((hr.eventually (gt_mem_nhds hε)).and (ht.and hst))).exists with
509:     ⟨n, hn, hrn, htn, hstn⟩
510:   set u : ℕ → Set X := fun j => ⋃ b ∈ decode₂ (ι n) j, t n b
511:   refine iInf₂_le_of_le u (by rwa [iUnion_decode₂]) ?_
512:   refine iInf_le_of_le (fun j => ?_) ?_
513:   · rw [ediam_iUnion_mem_option]
514:     exact iSup₂_le fun _ _ => (htn _).trans hrn.le
515:   · calc
516:       (∑' j : ℕ, ⨆ _ : (u j).Nonempty, m (ediam (u j))) = _ :=
517:         tsum_iUnion_decode₂ (fun t : Set X => ⨆ _ : t.Nonempty, m (ediam t)) (by simp) _
518:       _ ≤ ∑' i : ι n, m (ediam (t n i)) := ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun b => iSup_le fun _ => le_rfl
519:       _ ≤ c := hn.le
520: 
521: /-- To bound the Hausdorff measure (or, more generally, for a measure defined using
522: `MeasureTheory.Measure.mkMetric`) of a set, one may use coverings with maximum diameter tending to
523: `0`, indexed by any sequence of finite types. -/
524: theorem mkMetric_le_liminf_sum {β : Type*} {ι : β → Type*} [hι : ∀ n, Fintype (ι n)] (s : Set X)
525:     {l : Filter β} (r : β → ℝ≥0∞) (hr : Tendsto r l (𝓝 0)) (t : ∀ n : β, ι n → Set X)
526:     (ht : ∀ᶠ n in l, ∀ i, ediam (t n i) ≤ r n) (hst : ∀ᶠ n in l, s ⊆ ⋃ i, t n i) (m : ℝ≥0∞ → ℝ≥0∞) :
527:     mkMetric m s ≤ liminf (fun n => ∑ i, m (ediam (t n i))) l := by
528:   simpa only [tsum_fintype] using mkMetric_le_liminf_tsum s r hr t ht hst m

535: /-- Hausdorff measure on an (e)metric space. -/

542: theorem le_hausdorffMeasure (d : ℝ) (μ : Measure X) (ε : ℝ≥0∞) (h₀ : 0 < ε)
543:     (h : ∀ s : Set X, ediam s ≤ ε → μ s ≤ ediam s ^ d) : μ ≤ μH[d] :=
544:   le_mkMetric _ μ ε h₀ h

546: /-- A formula for `μH[d] s`. -/
547: theorem hausdorffMeasure_apply (d : ℝ) (s : Set X) :
548:     μH[d] s =
549:       ⨆ (r : ℝ≥0∞) (_ : 0 < r),
550:         ⨅ (t : ℕ → Set X) (_ : s ⊆ ⋃ n, t n) (_ : ∀ n, ediam (t n) ≤ r),
551:           ∑' n, ⨆ _ : (t n).Nonempty, ediam (t n) ^ d :=
552:   mkMetric_apply _ _

554: /-- To bound the Hausdorff measure of a set, one may use coverings with maximum diameter tending
555: to `0`, indexed by any sequence of countable types. -/
556: theorem hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum {β : Type*} {ι : β → Type*} [∀ n, Countable (ι n)]
557:     (d : ℝ) (s : Set X) {l : Filter β} (r : β → ℝ≥0∞) (hr : Tendsto r l (𝓝 0))
558:     (t : ∀ n : β, ι n → Set X) (ht : ∀ᶠ n in l, ∀ i, ediam (t n i) ≤ r n)
559:     (hst : ∀ᶠ n in l, s ⊆ ⋃ i, t n i) : μH[d] s ≤ liminf (fun n => ∑' i, ediam (t n i) ^ d) l :=
560:   mkMetric_le_liminf_tsum s r hr t ht hst _
561: 
562: /-- To bound the Hausdorff measure of a set, one may use coverings with maximum diameter tending
563: to `0`, indexed by any sequence of finite types. -/
564: theorem hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_sum {β : Type*} {ι : β → Type*} [∀ n, Fintype (ι n)]
565:     (d : ℝ) (s : Set X) {l : Filter β} (r : β → ℝ≥0∞) (hr : Tendsto r l (𝓝 0))
566:     (t : ∀ n : β, ι n → Set X) (ht : ∀ᶠ n in l, ∀ i, ediam (t n i) ≤ r n)
567:     (hst : ∀ᶠ n in l, s ⊆ ⋃ i, t n i) : μH[d] s ≤ liminf (fun n => ∑ i, ediam (t n i) ^ d) l :=
568:   mkMetric_le_liminf_sum s r hr t ht hst _

570: /-- If `d₁ < d₂`, then for any set `s` we have either `μH[d₂] s = 0`, or `μH[d₁] s = ∞`. -/
571: theorem hausdorffMeasure_zero_or_top {d₁ d₂ : ℝ} (h : d₁ < d₂) (s : Set X) :
572:     μH[d₂] s = 0 ∨ μH[d₁] s = ∞ := by
573:   by_contra! H
574:   suffices ∀ c : ℝ≥0, c ≠ 0 → μH[d₂] s ≤ c * μH[d₁] s by

31: /-- The diameter of a set in a pseudoemetric space as an extended nonnegative real number. -/
32: noncomputable def ediam (s : Set X) :=
33:   ⨆ (x ∈ s) (y ∈ s), edist x y
34: 
35: theorem ediam_eq_sSup (s : Set X) : ediam s = sSup (image2 edist s s) := sSup_image2.symm
36: 
37: theorem ediam_le_iff {d : ℝ≥0∞} : ediam s ≤ d ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, edist x y ≤ d := by
38:   simp only [ediam, iSup_le_iff]

40: theorem ediam_image_le_iff {d : ℝ≥0∞} {f : α → X} {s : Set α} :
41:     ediam (f '' s) ≤ d ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, edist (f x) (f y) ≤ d := by
42:   simp only [ediam_le_iff, forall_mem_image]
43: 
44: theorem edist_le_of_ediam_le {d} (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) (hd : ediam s ≤ d) : edist x y ≤ d :=
45:   ediam_le_iff.1 hd x hx y hy

47: /-- If two points belong to some set, their edistance is bounded by the diameter of the set -/
48: theorem edist_le_ediam_of_mem (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) : edist x y ≤ ediam s :=

value.justification: Taking epsilon=1 first excludes X=infinity. If X>0, epsilon=X/(2C) contradicts the bound. For the dimension bound, choosing q=D+1 first excludes Y=infinity. If finite Y>D+1, choose q=D+(Y-D-1)/2 to contradict Y≤q+1. The same midpoint argument gives the bound at 1 in the other branch. V is a delta-cover with finite positive delta, and A_i,B_i are its coordinate projections.

If B_i is nonempty, fixing b in B_i gives |t-b|≤rho_i for every t in B_i, so it lies in the bounded interval [b-rho_i,b+rho_i].

For nonempty W_i of positive diameter set U_i=W_i. If W_i={x}, set U_i to the open Euclidean ball centered at that unique x with diameter beta_i (radius beta_i/2). For empty W_i set U_i=empty.

value.text: Under L1: n=0, N002 gives E=R^0 and D=0. The coordinate map from I to F obtained by adjoining the unique R^0 coordinate preserves all distances. Fix arbitrary a under L4: a>1. N003 gives H^a(I)=0, so by the defining infimum there are covers of I at every positive scale with arbitrarily small a-cost. Push these covers forward by that coordinate map; their diameters are unchanged, so H^a(F)=0. N001 gives dim_H(F)≤a. Let the arbitrary a decrease to 1 to obtain dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. Discharge L4 and L1 and record F000.

value.text: For the other branch introduce L2: n≥1. Fix arbitrary q under L3: q>D, and arbitrary positive delta and epsilon. N002 gives D≥0, so q>0. Define r=min(1,delta/sqrt(2))>0; thus r≤1 and sqrt(2)r≤delta. By N001 applied to E, H^q(E)=0. The nonnegative content H^q_r(E) is at most this supremum, hence zero. The infimum defining that content therefore supplies a countable r-cover W with total q-cost<epsilon/2. The infimum is zero, so its admissible family is nonempty (an empty infimum is infinity); its defining approximation property gives the stated cover. This is the existence statement F001, before choosing W.

value.text: Choose W from F001. Define beta,U,K,r_i as declared. A nonempty zero-diameter Euclidean set is a singleton. Because n≥1, its replacement open ball has positive diameter beta_i≤r and q-cost beta_i^q≤epsilon*2^(-i-3)<epsilon*2^(-i-2). Nonempty positive-diameter members are unchanged; every point originally covered remains covered. The additional cost is at most sum_{i≥0}epsilon*2^(-i-3)=epsilon/4<epsilon/2. Thus, after discarding empty members by restricting to K, U is a countable cover of E with 0<r_i≤r and sum_{i∈K}r_i^q<epsilon. This is F002; the countable index set may be finite.

produces.statement: The family (U_i)_(i∈K) covers E, 0<r_i≤r≤1 for i∈K, r_i=diam(U_i), and sum_(i∈K)r_i^q<epsilon.

value.text:
For i∈K define N_i=ceil(1/r_i). Divide I into N_i closed intervals, each of length 1/N_i≤r_i. Since r_i≤1, N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i. The products of U_i with these intervals form a countable cover of F. The Euclidean distance formula in D006 shows that every product member has diameter at most sqrt(2)r_i≤sqrt(2)r≤delta. Their total (q+1)-cost is bounded by
sum_(i∈K) N_i (sqrt(2)r_i)^(q+1)
≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1) sum_(i∈K) r_i^q
<2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon.
These inequalities follow termwise from N_i≤2/r_i and then by nonnegative summation, so they remain valid for countably many members. Consequently H^(q+1)_delta(F)≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon, which is F003.

value.text: For fixed q and delta, epsilon>0 was arbitrary; the content in F003 is independent of epsilon, so it is zero. Since delta>0 was arbitrary, H^(q+1)(F)=0. Since q>D was arbitrary and D is finite by N002, let q decrease to D to obtain dim_H(F)≤D+1: an alleged strict excess would allow a q between D and dim_H(F)-1, contradicting this bound (an infinite dimension is already excluded by any one q>D). Empty members may be discarded; equivalently retain them with all ensuing projections and intervals empty and costs zero. Define rho,A_i,B_i and c as declared. Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz for the Euclidean metric in D006: each squared coordinate distance is bounded by the sum of the squared horizontal and vertical distances. Hence diam(A_i),diam(B_i)≤rho_i≤delta. In particular a nonempty B_i is a nonempty bounded subset of R. N002 applies to the positive s,delta and gives c<infinity.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary epsilon>0 and set eta_i=epsilon*2^(-i-1)/(1+rho_i^s)>0. Define J as declared. For a nonempty B_i, its supremum minus its infimum equals its diameter and is at most rho_i by F001. Thus B_i⊆J_i and |J_i|≤rho_i+eta_i. The empty-member convention makes both assertions true for empty V_i as well. The J_i are open measurable sets and enclose the possibly nonmeasurable projections. argument.text: Define the nonnegative functions f_i(t)=rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t). They are measurable because each J_i is open and each coefficient is a fixed finite nonnegative real. Under L2: t∈I, for every x∈E the point (x,t) lies in F, so some V_i contains it. Then x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. Thus the family of A_i with t∈J_i is a delta-cover of E, and the defining infimum and diam(A_i)≤rho_i give c≤sum_i rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t)=sum_i f_i(t). The point x here is universally bound in this coverage argument, and i is its existential cover index. Discharge L2 into the assertion for every t∈I. Record F003.

argument.text:
Set μ=λ|I. It is a measure on the Borel real line with μ(R)=λ(I)=1. Apply M006 with α=R, its Borel structure, index type β=N, this measure μ and the functions f of F003. Borel measurability implies μ-almost-everywhere measurability for each summand. Monotonicity of the nonnegative integral and the integral of a constant on a set of measure one give
c≤∫_I sum_i f_i(t) dλ

Finally eta_i rho_i^s=epsilon*2^(-i-1)*rho_i^s/(1+rho_i^s)≤epsilon*2^(-i-1), whose sum is epsilon. All sums and integrals are nonnegative and may be infinite; c is finite by F001. This is F004.

Moreover these contents are nondecreasing as scale decreases, since a cover admissible at a smaller scale is admissible at any larger one. argument.text: Temporarily assume L1: D=0. By H002 choose x_0∈E and define f(t)=(x_0,t). The Euclidean metric formula in D006 gives dist(f(t),f(u))=|t-u| for all real t,u, including n=0. Thus f restricts to an isometric embedding of I into F.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary s under L2: 0<s<1. For any delta>0 and arbitrary V under L3: V is a delta-cover of F, define W as declared. F001 shows W covers I, and isometry gives diam(W_i)≤diam(V_i)≤delta. Hence H^s_delta(I)≤sum_i diam(V_i)^s. Take the infimum over V, discharge L3, and then take the supremum over positive delta to get H^s(I)≤H^s(F). N002 gives finite D≥0. Thus either D>0 or D=0. In the positive case N006 gives dim_H(F)≥D+1; in the zero case N007 gives the identical bound, including n=0. N004 supplies dim_H(F)≤D+1 in all cases.
